clue.text: Mislays a card and gets discouraged

parts.note: to mislay something is to lose it, so 'mislays' gives loses
a heart is a playing card from the red suit

explanation.surface: A careless card player drops one from their hand and grows downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a card' looks like any card, but one particular suit is meant: a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom for becoming dispirited or discouraged.

clue.text: Something carried off in sacking

parts.note: sacking reads like the coarse cloth of a bag, but it is the plundering of a captured town, and what is carried off is the plunder

explanation.surface: Goods hauled away in a hessian bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder seized when a town is sacked is the classic sense of the word.

clue.text: Whiskies giving you courage?

definitions.meaning: courage here is morale, as in keeping up one's mood and pluck

explanation.surface: A dram or two is the drinker's remedy for nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Dutch courage, the boldness drink brings; the two senses are strong drink and morale.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled drinks are called by the same word as one's mood or pluck, as in 'in good heart'.

clue.text: Salvation Army boy bringing troops into line? The sauce!

parts.note: a boy is a lad
dressing ranks is the drill term for aligning soldiers in a straight line

explanation.surface: An officer drills a Salvationist youth with the soldiers, and someone exclaims at the cheek of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sauce!' reads as an exclamation at someone's impudence, but it is the definition: a sauce poured on a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette and mayonnaise are sauces put on leaves, and so are salad dressings.

clue.text: Awful pains in fractured leg — then passing away

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the scrambled pains is placed within the other scrambled word
a fractured leg is broken, so its three letters are rearranged
awful pains suggests a messed-up version of that word, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A patient with a broken leg suffers terrible pain and then dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' and 'fractured' each signal a rearrangement, of pains and leg respectively; 'in' says the first lies inside the second. The surface's hospital scene hides the definition, a quiet word for time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that is elapsing is going by, slipping away.

clue.text: I rose awkwardly for her

indicators.note: rising awkwardly suggests a clumsy jumble, so the letters of 'I rose' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stood up clumsily as a gesture to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' is the definition: a girl's name, which a female pronoun stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name can be defined as 'her', standing for any woman.

clue.text: Two articles girl produced

parts.note: the definite article is the, the indefinite one is a; the phrase gives both
the definite article is the, the indefinite one is a; the phrase gives both

explanation.surface: A girl wrote a couple of pieces for a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests pieces of writing, but they are the grammatical articles.
explanation.definitionFit: A short female name, so it fits the generic 'girl'.

clue.text: Fish in hail-storm from upended tub

indicators.note: a storm whips the word hail about, so its letters are rearranged
a tub turned upside down in a down clue reads from the bottom up

explanation.surface: A fish turns up in a hailstorm, tipped out of an overturned tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' turns HAIL into HALI; 'upended' turns TUB into BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish of northern seas.

clue.text: Though far from professional, I rush around after a colleague

indicators.note: the jumbled I rush is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: a mate is a workmate or colleague

indicators.note: the words I rush are thrown around, so their letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their hurried work as they dash about behind a coworker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals that I RUSH is scrambled, and 'after' places that jumble behind the colleague; 'Though' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, unskilled work is described as that of a non-professional or dabbler.

clue.text: Gold that is one side of the window

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
L for left, one side of anything

explanation.surface: Something gilded sits on one side of a window.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting bay window on an upper floor.

clue.text: America is involved with a winding trail leading to another place

indicators.note: a winding trail twists about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: USA is America

explanation.surface: An American hiker follows a twisting path to a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges USA + A + TRAIL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is simply a place other than here, a deliberately vague definition.

clue.text: Progressing like most rivers, we hear — coming to dead end then losing usefulness

indicators.note: says the phrase is taken by its sound, with the last word spelt differently

parts.note: most rivers flow toward the ocean, so they are running to the sea

indicators.note: the end of the word dead is its final letter

explanation.surface: Rivers flowing on, heard reaching a dead end, then going to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNNING TO SEA said aloud gives RUNNING TO SEE; 'coming to' adds D, the end of 'dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable that bolts to flower is no longer good to eat, hence the idiom for decline.

clue.text: Inscribed line wantonly observed — can't make it out

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective meaning too faint to be seen

indicators.note: wantonly suggests unrestrained disorder, so the letters of inscribed line are scrambled

explanation.surface: A carelessly engraved line is examined, but nobody can read it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wantonly' scrambles INSCRIBED LINE, all thirteen letters; 'observed' links it to the definition: when observed, one can't make it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too faint or unclear to perceive cannot be distinguished by the eye.

clue.text: Something in a shell curates can find addled

indicators.note: addled means muddled, so the letters of curates can are shuffled

explanation.surface: Muddled clergy find something hidden in a shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'addled' rearranges CURATES CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, lobsters and shrimps are hard-shelled creatures.

clue.text: After the interval comes round to fix damaged harp

indicators.note: places the ring after the rest

parts.note: a rest is an interval or pause, as in music
a ring is round, a circle

explanation.surface: A harpist mends a broken harp in the concert interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the circle behind the pause; 'interval' and 'harp' make a musical scene, so the solver reaches for a musical rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting new strings is how a musical instrument with broken strings is repaired.

clue.text: More suited to be a mechanic

definitions.meaning: comparative of fit, meaning better suited
an engineer who assembles or adjusts machinery

explanation.surface: Someone better qualified for a garage job.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of fit for better suited, and a noun for one who fits machine parts.

clue.text: Yacht in Southend could be called Jacinth

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: read as South end: the end of South is its last letter, H

explanation.surface: A boat moored at a seaside town on the Thames estuary could be named after a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTHEND is a resort town on the Thames estuary; read it as 'South end', giving H.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacinth is an old name for the reddish gemstone also called by the flower's name.

clue.text: Poet Laureate wearing symbol of rank over shoulder seems to have gone overboard

indicators.note: one piece wears the other, so the abbreviation sits inside

parts.note: a sash is a band worn across the shoulder as a mark of rank
PL is the abbreviation for Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A Poet Laureate in his sash seems to have fallen off a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' says the poet's abbreviation goes inside the band of rank; the definition describes the noise of someone falling into water.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy plunge into water is what you hear when someone falls off a boat.

clue.text: Deceives by dawdling, thus keeps out of sight

parts.note: to lie is to deceive
dawdling means going slow

explanation.surface: A liar, slow to move, hides away.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break shifts: LIE + SLOW reads as LIES LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay hidden or inconspicuous is an idiom meaning to avoid notice.

clue.text: With which to observe ginger-headed girl?

definitions.text: With which to observe ginger-headed girl?

parts.note: to eye is to observe

indicators.note: ginger-headed read as the head, the first letter, of ginger

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Something to ogle a red-haired young woman with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger-headed' looks like red hair but gives G, the head of 'ginger'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle or lens for one eye is used to look at things closely.

clue.text: Runner allowed in wrong heat

indicators.note: the synonym for allowed is put inside the jumbled heat
heat set wrong is mixed up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A runner is permitted to compete in the wrong heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges heat and 'in' puts the synonym for allowed inside it; the racing surface keeps 'Runner' looking literal, which it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is one kind of sportsperson competing on the track.

clue.text: New World clergyman? That's material

parts.note: the New World is the Americas
the cloth is a term for the clergy

explanation.surface: A churchman from across the Atlantic makes a joke about fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is the clergy as a body, after clerical dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilcloth with a glazed coating, a fabric used for table covers.

clue.text: Wandering Italian lost in Mongolian mountains

indicators.note: wandering means straying about, so these letters are jumbled
the letters of in are lost from the mixture

explanation.surface: A traveller from Italy gets lost in the mountains of Mongolia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' scrambles ITALIAN and 'lost' takes out the I and N of 'in', leaving the five letters of the range.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain range across Mongolia, Russia, China and Kazakhstan.

clue.text: A course at Oxford

parts.note: a course looks like a degree programme, but it is a watercourse: the name the Thames goes by as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: A programme of study at the university.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the Thames at Oxford has its own local name, after an Egyptian goddess.

clue.text: I lengthen flex to provide illumination

indicators.note: to flex is to bend, so the letters of I lengthen are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An electrician extends the cable so the lamp can reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flex' looks like a British word for an electric cable, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed light on, literally or by explaining.

clue.text: Dams restricting river vessels

indicators.note: one piece restricts, or encloses, the other

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, and ewes are mother sheep

explanation.surface: Barriers holding back a river's boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dams' suggests barriers, but it means mothers, here sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug or pitcher, typically for water, is a vessel.

clue.text: Information homing in from all directions

definitions.text: Information homing in from all directions

parts.words: Information homing in from all directions
parts.note: reports arrive from north, east, west and south, and the initials of those compass points spell the word

explanation.surface: Reports flooding in from everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports of recent events, popularly said to come from the four points of the compass.

clue.text: Send rights issue for overnight cover

indicators.note: an issue sends the letters out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Issuing rights for overnight insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' rearranges SEND RIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn in bed, covering the body at night.
